title: How to review and adjust your savings plan every quarter
description: The 'CFO Meeting' you need to have with yourself to stay on track.
content:
A financial plan is not a 'set and forget' document; it is a living strategy. Life changes fast—you get a raise, your rent goes up, the market crashes, or you decide to get married. If you only look at your finances once a year (at tax time), you are steering the ship with a blindfold. The most successful savers treat their personal finances like a business, holding a 'Quarterly Board Meeting' to review metrics, cut waste, and pivot strategy.

Key Takeaways

  • The 90-Day Cadence: Quarterly is the sweet spot. Monthly is too noisy (too much fluctuation); Annually is too slow to catch mistakes.
  • Net Worth Check: Update your balance sheet. Are assets up? Are liabilities down? The trend matters more than the number.
  • The Subscription Purge: Review credit card statements for 'Zombie Subscriptions' that crept in over the last 3 months.
  • Rebalancing: Check your asset allocation. If stocks rallied, you might need to trim and buy bonds.

Why It Matters (US Context)

US financial quarters (Q1-Q4) align with tax deadlines (Estimated Taxes) and corporate earnings. Syncing your personal review with these dates (April 1, July 1, Oct 1, Jan 1) helps you catch tax-loss harvesting opportunities and IRA contribution deadlines.

The Quarterly Agenda

Schedule 1 hour on the first Saturday of the new quarter. Follow this agenda.

1. The Net Worth Update

Log into your aggregator (Monarch/Empower).
Question: Did it go up? If not, why? (Market drop? High spending?).
Action: Record the number. Seeing progress motivates you.

2. The Cash Flow Audit

Look at your 'Savings Rate' for the last 3 months.
Target: 20%.
Actual: 12%.
Why: "Oh, we went on that trip and bought new tires."
Fix: Tighten the belt for the next quarter to average it out.

3. The Investment Checkup

Login to Fidelity/Vanguard.
Drift: Is your target 80/20 but you are now 85/15?
Fees: Did you accidentally buy a high-fee fund?
Cash Drag: Do you have $5,000 sitting in 'settled cash' that you forgot to invest? (Common mistake). Invest it.

Strategic Pivots

  1. Increase Automation: If you got a raise or paid off a debt this quarter, increase your auto-transfer immediately. Capture the cash flow before lifestyle creep sets in.
  2. Check Beneficiaries: Did you get married, divorced, or have a kid this quarter? Update your 401(k) beneficiaries. This overrides your will.
  3. Credit Report Scan: Check AnnualCreditReport.com (free). Look for new accounts you didn't open (Identity Theft).
  4. Tax Projection: In Q3 (October), estimate your income. Are you on track to owe the IRS? Increase 401(k) contributions now to lower your tax bill before Dec 31.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I need to rebalance every quarter?

Only if the drift is large (>5%). If you are 81% stocks and target is 80%, leave it. Frequent trading increases taxes. Only act on big moves.

Should I do this with my spouse?

Yes. The 'Wine and Wealth' night. Make it a date. Review the numbers together. It aligns your goals and reduces money arguments.

What if my Net Worth went down?

If the market crashed, that is normal. Focus on what you control: Savings Rate. Did you save enough? If yes, you won the quarter, even if the market lost.
